raw_segments.text: This was one of very many things that Kodak learned, and he was always learning.
Makka taught him to follow the cod and the halibut along the undersea banks and wrench
the rockling out of his hole among the weeds.
How to skirt the wrecks lying a hundred fathoms below water and dart like a rifle bullet in
at one porthole and out at another as the fishes ran.
How to dance on the top of the waves when the lightning was racing all over the sky
and wave his flipper politely to the stumpy-tailed albatross and the man o' war hawk as they
How to jump three or four feet clear of the water like a dolphin, flippers close to the
To leave the flying fish alone because they are all bony.
To take the shoulder piece out of a cod at full speed ten fathoms deep and never to stop
and look at a boat or a ship, but particularly a rowboat.
